evals.name: Python Harness Scaffolding
evals.prompt: I want to scaffold a standard-library-only Python harness in my project. What files should be created and what is the bootstrap command?
evals.expected_output: python -m skills.scripts.scaffold_harness --target /path/to/project, creating templates like harness.py, persistence.py, and context_manager.py
expectations: Mentions running python -m skills.scripts.scaffold_harness
Lists 7 template files: harness.py, context_manager.py, tool_registry.py, persistence.py, hooks.py, subagent.py, prompt_assembly.py
Emphasizes zero external dependencies rule
Templates are placed in the target project's harness directory

evals.name: Python Concurrency Safety Check
evals.prompt: Explain how the Python tool registry dynamically classifies shell commands to prevent dangerous execution.
evals.expected_output: Classification of commands into READ_ONLY, WORKSPACE_WRITE, and FULL_ACCESS with interactive approval for destructive commands
expectations: Explains the difference between static tool permissions and dynamic command classification
Lists safe read-only commands: ls, git status, cat, grep
Lists restricted full-access commands: rm -rf, sudo, curl, shutdown
Explains prompt approval mechanism for escalations

evals.name: Replay-Based Session Durability
evals.prompt: How does persistence.py guarantee that the agent session is restorable after a process crash?
evals.expected_output: Append-only JSON Line logging with immediate file flushes, plus replay loop reconstruction
expectations: Explains append-only JSON Line logging format
Mentions that every event calls flush() to guarantee it is written to disk instantly
Describes the replay loop reading the JSON lines sequentially to rebuild history
Points out that it is safe from process crash state losses

evals.name: Context Compaction Trigger
evals.prompt: My Python harness exceeds the token limit in long chats. How do I setup context compaction?
evals.expected_output: ContextManager class token estimation, threshold detection (e.g. 80%), and system-summarized old turns preservation
expectations: Describes character-word heuristics for token estimation in standard library
Explains the 80% threshold compaction trigger
Mentions keeping system prompt and recent N turns verbatim
Summarizes middle conversation turns into a system message summary block

evals.name: Workspace Hook Isolation
evals.prompt: How do I secure lifecycle hooks in Python so that third-party hooks do not execute in untrusted workspaces?
evals.expected_output: Workspace trust boundary checking in HookRegistry, all-or-nothing hook execution gating
expectations: Explains the all-or-nothing hook execution constraint
If workspace is untrusted, all local pre/post hooks are skipped entirely
Only hardcoded validation checks run in untrusted mode
Prevents arbitrary execution of malicious hooks from cloned repositories

evals.name: Sub-agent Recursion Gate
evals.prompt: How does the Python sub-agent implementation prevent exponential context cost explosions?
evals.expected_output: Enforces single-level spawning invariant by excluding the spawn_subagent tool from child registries
expectations: Mentions the 'Fork children must not fork' design invariant
Restricts the sub-agent's registry from including the spawn_subagent tool
Ensures child context is summarized and returned to parent while discarding chat logs

evals.name: Prefix Caching Assembly
evals.prompt: How does the prompt assembler dynamically construct system prompts without breaking LLM caching?
evals.expected_output: Prefix-caching friendly aggregation putting static prompt first and dynamic guidelines second
expectations: Mentions searching ancestor directories for CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
Puts the static base prompt at the very beginning
Appends dynamic project guidelines files at the end of prompt
Explains how changing instructions at the start invalidates prefix caching

evals.name: Python Harness Validation
evals.prompt: Assess a Python project harness using the validate_harness.py script. What metrics are scored?
evals.expected_output: Execution of validate_harness.py checking Instructions, State, Verification, Scope, and Lifecycle subsystems
expectations: Mentions validate_harness.py command line usage
Lists 5 scored subsystems: Instructions, State, Verification, Scope, Lifecycle
Checks for key artifacts: AGENTS.md, feature_list.json, progress.md, init.sh
Explains score threshold (min-score default 70) and exit codes

evals.name: Verification Commands Detection
evals.prompt: My Python agent needs to run test verification before submission. How does the harness verify success?
evals.expected_output: Subprocess execution of py_compile syntax checks and pytest suites
expectations: Specifies py_compile for checking syntax
Specifies pytest or unittest command execution
Captures stdout, stderr, and non-zero exit codes to fail fast
Logs evidence to the session history

evals.name: Harness Scaffolding Audit
evals.prompt: Run the scaffold_harness.py script to initialize a harness in a target project. How is the target directory structured?
evals.expected_output: Scaffolding of templates directory into the target's harness folder, preserving module layout
expectations: Scaffolds templates into target folder
Preserves imports structure for submodules
Supports --force flag to overwrite existing files
Verifies directory writes successfully
